question: Does subsequent Ram retail growth coexist with stable or falling inventory and no greater incentive intensity?
scope: Six discovery queries followed by selective source reading. Q2 2026 retail sales aligned with June 2026 advertised offers and end-June inventory context. No paid data, VIN scraping or additional agents.
result: Retail recovery confirmed for 1500; the joint test of inventory normalization and reduced incentive dependence remains unproven. Close bounded Ram investigation with this limitation.

offers25.locator: Ram 1500 and Ram Heavy Duty sections

1500_June2025.finance: As low as 1.9% APR / 72 months, excludes RHO

1500_June2026.finance: As low as 0% / 60 months, 2.9% / 72 months, 4.9% / 84 months; excludes RHO

offer_comparison.interpretation: Promotional support persists. Cash maxima alone suggest +$500 for 1500, but 2025 employee pricing and different loan terms prevent ranking total offer generosity. Same 72-month promotional APR is higher in 2026. No defensible average incentive-spending change can be calculated.
limitations: Offers are maxima/minima, not realized averages.
Eligibility, geography, trim, model year and credit quality may differ.
Do not assume cash, employee pricing, loyalty and subsidized APR all stack.
Model-year coverage is not explicit in 2026 offer heading.
Presence of 0% financing does not prove demand failure or increasing subsidy cost.

checks_and_limits: Retail +9% is distinct from total pickup +14%; no substitution of fleet-inclusive growth for consumer growth.
June offers coincide with quarter-end but do not measure the full-quarter weighted incentive burden.
Brand inventory and model retail populations differ; cannot treat this as a fully matched panel.
Days supply combines inventory and recent selling pace; it does not by itself establish inventory accumulation.
June Cox example of incentives at 6.7% of ATP belongs to Jeep, not Ram; excluded from Ram inference.
No matched national 1500 inventory-unit series or incentive/transaction-price panel retrieved.
No latest-period HD retail growth verified in this pass.
A secondary report was used only to locate the original Cox release. Reddit snippets were not used as validated results.
model_implication: Observed retail growth supports volume recovery. Do not infer restored pricing power, a normalized dealer stock position, or a launch-only explanation. Keep volume and net-price/margin assumptions separate; no new numerical forecast calibration from these offer snapshots.
stopping_decision: Close the Ram discovery pass. Resume only for new clean model-level evidence or a specific modeling need; otherwise proceed to another model.
